name: LSSP
description: Research artifact archive for "How Portable Are LLM-Serving Scheduler Rankings Across Workloads, Operating Regions, and Metrics?" (Soroush Vahidi). LSSP measures whether comparative LLM-serving scheduler rankings transfer across independent workload sources, operating regions, evaluation metrics, and SLO definitions, and whether a simulator's ranking conclusions transfer to real hardware. This archive is the exact source snapshot of GitHub release v1.0.0 (commit 18128a8cf4d449c333c6db4d31788dd5eae180bd): simulator and 13-policy scheduler library, real-vLLM RQ6 engineering infrastructure, frozen Phase-10/11/12 hash-identified manifests, manuscript source and compiled PDF, RQ6 public result/provenance documentation, reproducibility docs, and the 378-test test suite. Scientific scope (all complete): RQ1-RQ5 (13-policy simulator panel, 3 independently sourced workloads x 6 calibrated load regions x 2 repetitions = 18,720 structurally validated cells) plus RQ6, a selected-case physical vLLM 0.27.1 / A100 validation: 240/240 real executions completed and independently validated (2 policies x 3 sources x 40 independent workload windows/source, 200 requests/window, one execution per cell; window-level paired bootstrap, 2,000 resamples). The simulator-predicted Azure/BurstGPT reversal did not reproduce on physical hardware; the Azure/Bailian-Qwen stable control was qualitatively retained.
